## Why

P34.44a built the quality system — the 27-check registry, the ratchet
engine, the read-only harness — but nothing yet *measures production*
or holds a measured gain. This row delivers the two halves that turn
the registry into a signal: the hosted L2 baseline run (which also sets
the ratchet baselines from measured values, never from prose) and the
permanent nightly `sig-quality-probe` job that runs the spine-probe (M)
checks off-peak, writes a `probe-run/1` per run and alerts the operator
on failure. Both live legs are window- and dependency-gated; this PR
lands the engineering — declaration, engine, in-container verbs, the
IaC leg, the alert-path IAM — and queues the mutations honestly.

## What ships

- **`ops/quality_probe.toml` — `sig.quality-probe/1`**: the declaration
  of the permanent `sig-quality-probe` Cloud Run job — `sh -c 'exec
  sig-ops quality nightly'`, 1 task, **0 retries**, 1800 s, 1 CPU / 2
  Gi, the `sig-pg`/`sig` Cloud SQL connector, the restricted-bucket
  prefix `ops/probes/quality/`, alert kind `quality-probe`, the plain
  env allow-list, and exactly two secret bindings
  (`SIG_AUDIT_PASSWORD`, `SIG_ALERT_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`) — plus the
  `sig-sched-quality-probe` trigger `0 1 1-5,14-31 * *` Etc/UTC with the
  `sig-scheduler` invoker.
- **`ops/src/ops/quality_job.py`** — the declaration engine: fail-closed
  TOML load + validation (names, SA/env/prefix/timeout shapes,
  task/retry posture, secret pins); the shared window predicates
  (`in_quiet_hours`, `in_batch_window`, `suppression_reason`,
  `leg_window_reason`); a **structural schedule proof** —
  `validate_schedule` computes a year of cron fires and refuses a
  schedule that can land inside either window; the exact `gcloud` argv
  renderers (deploy, invoker binding, trigger create/update/URI,
  rollback); and `verify_describe`/`verify_trigger` — describe-vs-
  declaration judges that require a digest-pinned image (`:latest` or a
  tag ref is a finding) and check the whole posture (tasks, retries,
  timeout, one container, secret-env allow-list, no `envFrom`, Cloud SQL
  connector; schedule, timezone, URI, POST, OAuth SA, not paused).
- **`sig-ops quality nightly`** — the job's container command: applies
  the same suppression predicate the declaration proves (a suppressed
  run writes a `suppressed` `sig.probe-run/1` **without opening a DB
  connection**), otherwise opens the read-only `sig_audit`-posture
  session, runs the M placement, writes `sig.quality-report/1` +
  `sig.probe-run/1` locally and/or under the conditioned prefix, and
  alerts on failure or a breached band unless `--no-alert`. A failed
  run still writes an `error` probe-run — the run is never silent.
- **`sig-ops quality baseline`** — the L2 baseline run: every M and R
  check once each over the read-only session and a bounded read-only
  fetch of the current public release files; emits
  `sig.quality-baseline/1` (run id, target, per-check L2 reference vs
  measured, tolerance, findings) plus the ratchet proposal; uploads
  under `ops/probes/quality-baseline/`; **exits 3 when no ratchet check
  is measured** — fail-closed (SIG-ENG-042).
- **`exports/quality.py` + `sig-exports quality apply-baselines`** —
  measured-baseline application: `baseline_run`/`baseline_at`
  provenance on `QualityCheck` (paired or neither, `YYYY-MM-DD`,
  numeric baseline required when provenance exists);
  `baseline_proposal` (`baselined`/`tightened`/`kept`/
  `regression_kept`/`not_measured` — a regression is a recorded finding
  and **never loosens** the baseline; unknown checks refuse);
  `apply_baselines` rewrites only the touched check blocks, then
  **re-validates and re-diffs** the result so a loosening can never be
  written; `sig.quality-baseline-apply/1` records every apply.
- **`ops/gcp/quality-probe.sh`** — the windowed live leg: `--check`
  (no ADC, no network, prints every planned command, exit 0),
  `--apply` (window check **before** ADC, then `deps` — runtime SA,
  `sig_audit` login, both secrets, bucket versioning — before any
  mutation; a missing dep refuses the whole apply), `--verify`
  (poststate describe checks, plus `--from-state` offline replay),
  `--rollback` (pauses + deletes trigger and job by exact name,
  removes only the leg's bindings, **preserves historical probe
  records**), `baseline` (the execution-host pattern → `exec sig-ops
  quality baseline --emit`). Queued legs exit 42 with the re-run
  prompt.
- **IAM + config** — `sig-quality-probe-rt` joins the `sig-alerts`
  jobs-leg invoker grant and consumes `sig-alert-webhook-token`
  (least-privilege shape preserved, verified by the jobs-leg plan
  tests); `ops/gcp/config.sh` exports the `SIG_QUALITY_*` surface.
- **ADR-205** — the nightly-job shape (schedule, zero retries, read-only
  posture, append-only records, alert path) and the measured-baseline
  application rule; Appendix F row, ADR index, trigger register, BL-084
  home, CHANGELOG, `docs/build/reports/quality/` committed summary
  (marked QUEUED — measured counts land with the leg).
- **Tests** — `test_quality_job.py` (52), `test_quality_nightly.py`
  (19), `test_quality_baseline.py` (17), plus `test_gcp_iac.py` /
  `test_iam_identities.py` / `test_iam_job_identities.py` updates.

## Boundaries

Read-only end to end: the probe and baseline open one read-only session
(`default_transaction_read_only`, 60 s statement timeout — the
`sig_audit` posture); records are new objects under the conditioned
`ops/probes/` scope; the only registry writer is `apply-baselines`,
which re-diffs so a loosening is impossible; suppression never opens a
DB connection. `not_evaluable` is never a pass, `evaluated=0` fails, and
a failed run records before it alerts.
